title: Towards general auditory intelligence for machine listening and speaking - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Tsinghua-led review co-authored with Google DeepMind and NVIDIA researchers argues computer audition is being rebuilt on LLM foundations across four pillars — audio comprehension, audio generation, speech interaction and audio-visual understanding — with full-duplex, streaming speech dialogue as the defining engineering frontier. Note: the captured text is the open portion only (abstract, eight figure captions, a ~250-entry bibliography and author/funding disclosures); the body sits behind Nature's subscription wall, so insights below are drawn from those sections and from what the review's citation base reveals about the field's landscape.

insights.claim: Computer audition is being restructured around foundation models along four pillars — audio comprehension, audio generation, speech-based interaction and audio-visual understanding — rather than as separate ASR, TTS and sound-event pipelines.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Vendors still selling point ASR or TTS products are competing against consolidated audio-LLM stacks; expect margin compression in single-task speech tooling.
insights.quote: This Review provides a comprehensive review of recent progress in integrating audio into large language models, with a focus on four key areas: audio comprehension, audio generation, speech-based interaction and audio–visual understanding.

insights.claim: Audio is framed as a modality carrying semantic, emotional and contextual cues that are prerequisites for naturalistic and embodied machine intelligence, making voice an input requirement for robotics and agents rather than an optional interface layer.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Supports capex in audio sensing and on-device audio compute for robotics and agent hardware, not just for call-centre software.
insights.quote: Audio, as a modality rich in semantic, emotional and contextual cues, has a vital role in achieving naturalistic and embodied machine intelligence.

insights.claim: The review's closing citation is a 2026 ICLR paper titled 'End-to-end listen, look, speak and act', signalling that the intended destination of audio LLMs is embodied agents that perceive and act, not conversational chatbots.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Watch audio-conditioned action models as the next research-to-product hop after voice assistants.
insights.quote: End-to-end listen, look, speak and act
insights.locator: References — final entry, Wang, S. et al.

insights.claim: The review explicitly targets 'general auditory intelligence' as a stated end goal — systems that perceive, understand and interact through sound as naturally as humans — which sets an evaluation bar far above word error rate.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Legacy ASR accuracy benchmarks are no longer the competitive metric; paralinguistics, reasoning and turn-taking are.
insights.quote: building general auditory intelligence capable of perceiving, understanding and interacting through sound as naturally as humans do

themes.theme: Representation fork: tokens vs continuous features

insights.claim: The review devotes a dedicated figure to 'two paradigms for audio representation in LLMs', treating the discrete-token versus continuous-feature choice as the unresolved architectural fork of the field.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Codec-token vs continuous-feature bets determine inference cost and licensing dependencies; a wrong pick strands a product's serving stack.
insights.quote: Fig. 2: Two paradigms for audio representation in LLMs.

insights.claim: The debate is being settled empirically rather than by fiat — the bibliography includes a head-to-head study, 'Speech discrete tokens or continuous features? A comparative analysis for spoken language understanding in speech LLMs' (EMNLP 2025), alongside continuous audio language models at ICLR 2026.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Continuous-feature approaches re-entering top venues in 2026 suggests the codec-token orthodoxy of 2023-2024 is being challenged.
insights.quote: Speech discrete tokens or continuous features? A comparative analysis for spoken language understanding in speech LLMs

insights.claim: Neural audio codecs are the cost bottleneck of audio LLMs, and the cited stack (SoundStream, EnCodec, improved RVQGAN, Single-Codec, WavTokenizer, NanoCodec, FlexiCodec, finite scalar quantization) is being optimized explicitly for low frame rates and fast speech-LLM inference.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Frame-rate reductions in codecs translate directly into tokens-per-second and therefore GPU cost per minute of voice served — a key unit-economics lever for voice-agent providers.
insights.quote: NanoCodec: towards high-quality ultra fast speech LLM inference

insights.claim: The review cites encoder-free and monolithic multimodal designs (encoder-free vision-language models, Mono-InternVL) next to audio-encoder work, implying the separate audio encoder may eventually be absorbed into the LLM itself.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: If encoders collapse into the backbone, standalone speech-encoder IP (and the companies built on it) loses defensibility.
insights.locator: References — Diao, H. et al.; Luo, G. et al.

insights.claim: Architecture diversification beyond transformers has reached audio: the bibliography includes Mamba, state-space large audio language models, DuplexMamba for real-time duplex speech, and DIFFA (diffusion language models that listen).
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Linear-time sequence models are attractive for always-on streaming audio where attention cost scales badly — a watch item for edge voice silicon.
insights.locator: References — Gu, A. & Dao, T.; Bhati, S. et al.; Lu, X. et al.

themes.theme: Full-duplex voice as the engineering frontier

insights.claim: Three of the review's eight figures cover speech interaction, full-duplex dialogue architectures and streaming speech processing, indicating the authors treat real-time full-duplex conversation — not comprehension — as the field's hard problem.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Product differentiation in voice AI is shifting from transcription accuracy to interruption handling and latency — evaluate vendors on turn-taking, not WER.
insights.quote: Fig. 7: An overview of streaming speech processing with LLMs, which is the foundation for full-duplex dialogue.

insights.claim: The full-duplex system space is already crowded with named implementations — Moshi, SALMONN-omni, Mini-Omni, LLaMA-Omni2, Freeze-Omni, OmniFlatten, FlexDuo, FireRedChat, DuplexMamba and synchronous-LLM duplex agents — most published within roughly two years.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Full-duplex capability is commoditizing fast; startups pitching it as core IP have a short window before it is table stakes.
insights.quote: SALMONN-omni: a standalone speech LLM without codec injection for full-duplex conversation

insights.claim: 'Thinking while speaking' has become a distinct research subproblem, with cited work on chunked simultaneous reasoning (STITCH), token-level thinking-in-speaking (Mini-Omni-Reasoner), chronological thinking in full-duplex models and dual-brain mind-paced speaking.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The reasoning-versus-latency tradeoff is where voice agents will visibly differ; solving it unlocks reasoning-grade voice assistants without dead air.
insights.quote: Mind-paced speaking: a dual-brain approach to real-time reasoning in spoken language models

insights.claim: Latency engineering in speech LLMs is converging on specific tricks the review catalogues: multi-token prediction (VocalNet), interleaved cross-modal token generation (VITA-Audio), parallel text-and-speech generation (PSLM), frozen-LLM designs (Freeze-Omni) and dual-resolution speech representations (DrVoice).
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: These techniques cut tokens generated per second of speech, lowering the cost floor for always-on voice products and pressuring per-minute pricing.
insights.locator: References — Wang, Y. et al.; Long, Z. et al.; Mitsui, K. et al.

insights.claim: OpenAI's GPT-4o and gpt-realtime are cited as the commercial reference points for real-time voice, and open-source releases explicitly benchmark themselves against that bar (MiniCPM-O 2.6 and VITA-1.5 both marketed as 'GPT-4o level').
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Open-weight parity claims against GPT-4o voice compress OpenAI's realtime-API pricing power within a 12-18 month lag.
insights.quote: MiniCPM-O 2.6: a GPT-4o level MLLM for vision, speech, and multimodal live streaming on your phone

themes.theme: Who builds it: China-led open stack, US labs co-authoring

insights.claim: The author roster spans Tsinghua University's Department of Electronic Engineering, Google DeepMind (Mountain View), NVIDIA (Santa Clara) and the University of Cambridge, making this a joint China-US industry-academia position statement on audio AI rather than a purely academic survey.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: DeepMind and NVIDIA staff publicly co-signing an audio-LLM roadmap signals both firms see audio as a strategic modality, not a niche.
insights.quote: Google DeepMind, Mountain View, CA, USA

insights.claim: The review discloses that it received no industrial funding and was supported by China's National Natural Science Foundation (grant 62476151), with several industry-affiliated authors contributing in an individual research capacity.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
entities: National Natural Science Foundation of China
insights.so_what: Reduces the discount an investor should apply for vendor bias, while confirming Chinese state funding underwrites the audio-LLM research agenda.
insights.quote: This work was not supported by industrial funding.

insights.claim: Chinese-origin models dominate the cited open audio and speech stack — Qwen-Audio, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-TTS, Kimi-Audio, GLM-4-Voice, Baichuan-Audio, MiMo-Audio, CosyVoice and CosyVoice 2, Seed-ASR, Seed-TTS, MinMo and VITA.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The open-weight voice stack is largely China-supplied, setting a near-zero licence cost floor that Western voice-model vendors must price against.
insights.locator: References — Chu, Y. et al.; Ding, D. et al.; Zeng, A. et al.; Du, Z. et al.

insights.claim: The bibliography reaches into 2026 preprints and conferences (Qwen3-TTS technical report, FlexiCodec and multiple ICLR 2026 entries), showing the review was updated to cover releases right up to publication in August 2026.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The landscape map is current, so its gaps (see safety and evaluation themes) are live gaps, not stale ones.
insights.locator: References — Hu, H. et al., Qwen3-TTS technical report

insights.claim: Muyan-TTS is cited as a trainable text-to-speech model optimized for podcast scenarios built on a $50K budget, a concrete marker of how cheap competent speech synthesis training has become.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: At $50K per trained voice model, TTS is not a defensible moat — value migrates to distribution, rights and voice licensing.
insights.quote: Muyan-TTS: a trainable text-to-speech model optimized for podcast scenarios with a $50K budget

themes.theme: Evaluation fragmentation and the benchmark land grab

insights.claim: Audio-LLM evaluation has fragmented into dozens of competing benchmarks in under three years — MMAU, MMAU-Pro, MMAR, MMSU, AIR-Bench, AudioBench, AHELM, SAKURA, BLAB, SD-Eval, VoxDialogue plus voice-assistant suites VoiceBench, VocalBench, URO-Bench, SOVA-Bench, S2S-Arena and Full-duplex-bench.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: With no consensus leaderboard, vendor benchmark claims in voice AI are largely non-comparable — demand head-to-head evals before underwriting performance claims.
insights.locator: References — Sakshi, S. et al.; Yang, Q. et al.; Chen, Y. et al.

insights.claim: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2 expands spoken-language-model evaluation to 180 tasks, quantifying how wide the expected capability surface of an audio LLM has become.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A 180-task surface means generalist audio models will beat narrow vendors on breadth even where the narrow vendor wins single tasks.
insights.quote: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2: a collaboratively expanding benchmark for measuring the capabilities of spoken language models with 180 tasks

insights.claim: LLM-as-judge is displacing signal-processing metrics in audio evaluation: the review cites audio-aware LLMs as judges of speaking styles and audio LLMs as descriptive speech-quality evaluators alongside legacy PESQ, DNSMOS, Frechet audio distance and MUSHRA metrics.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Cheap automated audio judging collapses the cost of QA in speech products and undermines businesses selling human MOS panels.
insights.quote: Audio-aware large language models as judges for speaking styles

insights.claim: The field has published an explicit 'roadmap towards superhuman speech understanding using large language models', showing researchers now frame the target as exceeding human listening rather than matching transcription accuracy.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Superhuman audio understanding (spatial, paralinguistic, multi-speaker) opens surveillance, diagnostics and monitoring markets closed to human-parity systems.
insights.quote: Roadmap towards superhuman speech understanding using large language models

themes.theme: Failure modes, safety surface and reliability gap

insights.claim: Audio LLMs demonstrably fail by defaulting to text priors and hallucinating sound objects — cited work shows text bias when audio and text disagree, object hallucination in large audio-language models, and catastrophic forgetting of instruction-following in speech-aware models.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Enterprise voice deployments in compliance-sensitive settings need audio-grounding tests; the failure is silent because the model still produces fluent text.
insights.quote: When audio and text disagree: revealing text bias in large audio-language models

insights.claim: Audio opens a distinct jailbreak attack surface, with dedicated benchmarks already published — JALMBench, Jailbreak-AudioBench, AudioTrust — and work showing benign-sounding audio inputs can jailbreak audio-language models.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Voice-enabled agents inherit a new, under-tooled attack class; audio red-teaming and guardrail vendors have an unserved market.
insights.quote: When good sounds go adversarial: jailbreaking audio-language models with benign inputs

insights.claim: Bias in speech-integrated LLMs is documented as a specific research concern, with cited work on semantic gender bias in speech-integrated large language models and multi-accent handling for Indian languages.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Accent and gender performance gaps are the likeliest regulatory and reputational flashpoint for consumer voice products.
insights.quote: Listen and speak fairly: a study on semantic gender bias in speech integrated large language models

insights.claim: Reinforcement learning is being shown to beat supervised fine-tuning in audio question answering, and the review cites Audio-Thinker (RL for when and how to think) plus Omni-R1, which questions whether audio data is even needed to fine-tune an audio LLM.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: If text-only RL post-training transfers to audio tasks, the strategic value of proprietary labelled audio corpora falls sharply.
insights.quote: Omni-R1: do you really need audio to fine-tune your audio LLM?

insights.claim: Finance is already a named vertical for audio LLMs: the review cites FinAudio, a benchmark for audio large language models in financial applications, presented at a NeurIPS 2025 generative-AI-in-finance workshop.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Audio understanding of earnings calls and broker audio is being formally benchmarked — a direct path to alpha-generation tooling and a competitive threat to transcript-based data vendors.
insights.quote: FinAudio: a benchmark for audio large language models in financial applications

insights.claim: Clinical speech AI is flagged as a distinct responsible-development problem, with the review citing work on bridging the gap between clinical speech research and deployed technology in npj Digital Medicine.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Speech biomarkers are a regulated adjacency where evidence standards, not model quality, gate revenue.
insights.quote: Responsible development of clinical speech AI: bridging the gap between clinical research and technology
insights.locator: References — Berisha, V. & Liss, J. M.

insights.claim: Fusing audio with vision is presented as the route to situational awareness and cross-modal reasoning, backed by a dense cited lineage — video-SALMONN, video-SALMONN 2, video-SALMONN-o1, Video-LLaMA, VideoLLaMA 2, VAST, AVicuna and omni benchmarks WorldSense, Daily-Omni and Video-MME.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Video models without audio tracks are structurally handicapped on real-world understanding; audio-visual capability is a differentiator in video search, moderation and robotics.
insights.quote: Furthermore, we explore how the fusion of audio and visual modalities enhances situational awareness and cross-modal reasoning, pushing the boundaries of multimodal intelligence.

insights.claim: The review anchors machine listening in human auditory science — auditory scene analysis, cocktail-party effect, the Lombard sign, phonetic convergence and task-optimized networks that predict brain responses — implying architectural targets are drawn from human perception rather than from engineering convenience.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Human-perception benchmarks (multi-speaker, noisy, attentive listening) are the capability gaps most likely to define the next generation of audio models.
insights.locator: References — Bregman, A. S.; Arons, B.; Kell, A. J. et al.
